title: Non-Idempotent Reconciliation Operations
pattern: Processing events or queues with raw, non-idempotent inserts, forcing operators to execute manual reconciliation runs or patch database values later.
why_bad: Benign network retry events or duplications in MQ pipelines generate false-positive error logs, pollute transaction states, and require human operators to manually audit records [204, 642-645].
detection: Database writes in event consumer loops lacking uniqueness constraints or upsert logic.
fix: Enforce unique transactional idempotency keys on write endpoints, executing upserts or ignoring duplicates gracefully.
